citations.narrative:
The flooring of 5 outdoor runs of the sheltered housing facility was not being maintained in a manner that will protect the
dog's feet and legs from injury. The kennel utilizes greenhouse style flooring. There were holes in the flooring from
excessive wearing and chewing that resulted in large openings where the dogs' feet and legs could pass through and
cause injury, or could be a potential entry point for a predator. The holes measured were approximately 3"x 3" to 6" x 6".
Correct by ensuring that primary enclosures be constructed and maintained so that they have flooring that protects the
dogs' feet and legs from injury and the feet and legs cannot pass through the floor. Correct by November 21, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Additional Inspectors:
Autumn Glencamp, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
